data.name: Greece
data.summary: Ordinary residents pay 5% on dividends (final), 15% on gains from unlisted shares and from listed shares where they hold 0.5% or more, and nothing on listed shares below 0.5% or EU/EEA UCITS funds. Real estate CGT is suspended until 31 Dec 2026. Inheritance to children: first EUR 150,000 per child free, then 1% / 5% / 10%; lifetime parental gifts free up to a one-time EUR 800,000, then 10%. No wealth tax (ENFIA property tax only). New residents can instead pay a flat EUR 100,000 a year on all foreign income (Art. 5A Income Tax Code), plus EUR 20,000 per included family member, for up to 15 years, against a EUR 500,000 Greek investment.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation with separate schedular rates for investment income: 5% dividends, 15% interest, 15% capital gains on securities (with exemptions).
regimes.eligibility: Greek tax residence (physical presence over 183 days in any 12-month period, or centre of vital interests in Greece).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on listed shares are exempt if the seller holds less than 0.5% of the share capital; gains on non-listed shares, and on listed shares with a holding of 0.5% or more, are taxed at 15%. Gains on Greek and EU/EEA UCITS units are exempt. Greek-listed share sales bear a 0.1% sales tax. Real estate capital gains tax (15%) is suspended until 31 Dec 2026 (Art. 90 Law 5162/2024). Art. 42(1)(β) Law 4172/2013 taxes gains on listed shares only for holdings of 0.5% or more and names no particular exchange, so foreign-listed holdings below 0.5% are outside the charge (statute read on Taxheaven, 2026-10-16).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Below 0.5% holding in a listed company: exempt. EU/EEA UCITS: exempt.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Non-UCITS funds (e.g. US-domiciled ETFs) and bonds are not covered by the stated exemptions; treatment not verified. Real estate CGT suspension expires 31 Dec 2026; whether it is extended is unknown.

sources.title: Greece - Individual - Income determination

open_questions: Taxation of gains on non-UCITS ETFs and on bonds not verified.
Will the real estate CGT suspension be extended beyond 31 Dec 2026?

A 0.1% sales tax (Law 2579/1998) is reported to apply also to sales of shares listed on foreign regulated markets by sellers domiciled in Greece (Euronext Athens tax page, not opened); the projection has no tax on sale proceeds.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Portfolio holdings below 0.5% of any listed company: exempt. Private business: 15%. Real estate: 0 for disposals up to 31 Dec 2026 under the suspension (15% otherwise).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Frequent trading can be recharacterised as business income at progressive rates up to 44% (general principle; not verified in a source).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains under the same rules.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 5%. For Greek dividends the 5% withholding is final. Foreign dividends are taxed at 5% with credit for foreign tax up to the Greek tax (credit requires apostilled foreign tax documentation).

sources.title: Greece - Individual - Income determination
Greece - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

open_questions: Since treaty WHT (usually 15%) exceeds 5%, foreign dividends in practice bear foreign WHT only; the credit cannot exceed 5%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 5% on dividends paid by Greek companies (0% to EU parent companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive).
dividends.treaty_network: About 57 treaties including the US (count not verified).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets. Greek real estate is subject to the annual ENFIA (main tax per property plus a supplementary tax for individuals whose Greek real estate exceeds EUR 500,000).

sources.title: Greece - Individual - Other taxes (ENFIA)

open_questions: The ENFIA supplementary tax on total Greek real estate above EUR 500,000 is arguably a limited wealth tax on local real estate; its rates were not verified, so it is recorded as property tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: ENFIA: annual tax on Greek real estate held on 1 January; main tax per property plus supplementary tax where an individual's total exceeds EUR 500,000 (rates not verified). Main-residence reductions for insured persons. From 2027 a Local Development Fee (0.30-0.70 per mille) collected via energy bills (Law 5314/2026).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax (Law 2961/2001 as amended by Law 5219/2025). Children are Category A: first EUR 150,000 per heir tax-free, then 1% on the next EUR 150,000, 5% on the next EUR 300,000, 10% above EUR 600,000. Lifetime parental grants/gifts to children of any asset: a one-time EUR 800,000 tax-free allowance, then 10%. Cash gifts outside the parental grant regime: 10% for Category A. Immovable property abroad is never subject to Greek inheritance tax; movable assets abroad are taxable if the deceased was a Greek resident or national.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 150,000 per child on inheritance; EUR 800,000 one-time parental grant allowance per child.
inheritance.important_exceptions: New Succession Law 5303/2026 (deaths from 16 Sep 2026): inheritance contracts, waivers of future rights, forced share converted to a monetary claim; civil law, not tax.

sources.title: Greece - Individual - Other taxes (inheritance, gift and parental grant tax)

open_questions: Scope rule for foreign movable assets (Greek resident/national deceased) stated from general knowledge of Law 2961/2001 Art. 1; PwC only confirms foreign immovables are excluded.
Whether the parental-grant 10% above EUR 800,000 is flat or banded not confirmed beyond PwC wording.
inheritance.spouse_note: The spouse (or cohabitation-agreement partner) is Category A like children: first EUR 150,000 free, then 1% / 5% / 10% (about 9.9% effective on EUR 35 million, 10% marginal; Law 2961/2001 as amended by Law 5219/2025).
inheritance.gift_tax: Parental grants/gifts to children: one-time EUR 800,000 allowance per child, then 10%. Other gifts to Category A follow inheritance scales; cash gifts 10%.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Foreign real estate excluded. Foreign movable assets (securities) of a Greek-resident deceased are taxable (see open question). Art. 5A regime beneficiaries: see that regime.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Greek situs assets taxed regardless of nationality; foreign movables taxed where the deceased was a Greek national or resident.

regimes.name: Art. 5A alternative taxation of foreign income (EUR 100,000 flat)
regimes.description: Flat EUR 100,000 a year covering all foreign-source income (including foreign dividends and gains), regardless of amount, plus EUR 20,000 a year for each relative to whom the regime is extended (Art. 5A(2) Law 4172/2013). Foreign income need not be declared; foreign tax paid is not credited. Greek-source income taxed normally. Up to 15 tax years, not extendable (Art. 5A(4)). Movable property located abroad is exempt from Greek inheritance and gift tax, whether received or given by the beneficiary (Art. 5A(8)). Note: the brief called this Art. 5C; in the Income Tax Code the EUR 100,000 regime is Art. 5A, 5B is the 7% pensioner regime and 5C the 50% relief for workers.
regimes.eligibility: Not Greek tax resident in 7 of the 8 years before the transfer; transfer of tax residence to Greece; investment of at least EUR 500,000 (personally, by a relative, or through a majority-owned entity) in Greek real estate, businesses, securities or shares of Greek entities, completed within 3 years of the application; this condition is waived for holders of a Greek investor residence permit (golden visa, art. 16 Law 4251/2014) (Art. 5A(1)). Application to the Tax Administration with proof of transfer of the investment amount; individuals who moved in the previous tax year may also apply (Art. 5A(3)). Annual application deadline (reported as 31 March) not checked.

lump_sum.notes: Plus EUR 20,000 a year per relative to whom the regime is extended (Art. 5A(2)). Reference couple: EUR 100,000 + 1 x EUR 20,000 (spouse) = EUR 120,000 a year; the children have no foreign income and need not be included (their inheritance from the beneficiary is exempt under Art. 5A(8) as 'third parties'). A family of five with all four relatives included would pay EUR 100,000 + 4 x EUR 20,000 = EUR 180,000. Not indexed: the amounts change only by amendment. Paid in one instalment by the last working day of December; not offsettable. Greek-source income taxed separately. Non-payment ends the regime; if the EUR 500,000 investment is not completed within 3 years the regime is revoked from the start (Art. 5A(5)). The EUR 500,000 investment can be met by the Greek family home (real estate, personally or through a relative).

capital_gains.summary: Foreign capital gains are covered by the EUR 100,000 lump sum: payment of the lump sum exhausts every Greek tax liability on foreign-source income (Art. 5A(8)). Greek-source gains taxed as standard.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends covered by the lump sum: no Greek tax, and foreign withholding tax is not credited against any Greek liability (Art. 5A(2)). Greek dividends taxed at 5%.

Foreign real estate is outside Greek inheritance tax in any case. Greek-situs assets taxed under the standard Category A scale (EUR 150,000 free per child, then 1% / 5% / 10%).

open_questions: Art. 5A(2) also says inheritance, gift and parental-grant tax provisions 'do not apply' for relatives to whom the regime is extended; the exact scope of that sentence (e.g. Greek-situs assets) was not confirmed in guidance.
Whether the exemption survives for a death or gift after the 15-year period ends: the wording ties it to persons 'who have been subjected to' the regime; treated here as ending with the regime.
inheritance.spouse_note: Under Art. 5A(8) Law 4172/2013 the regime beneficiary's movable assets abroad passing to a spouse by death are exempt from Greek inheritance tax (deaths from 1 Jan 2020); Greek-situs assets use the standard Category A scale (EUR 150,000 free, then 1% / 5% / 10%).
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts of movable property located abroad made or received by the beneficiary while under the regime are exempt (Art. 5A(8)); Greek-situs assets as standard.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Movable property abroad (e.g. a foreign securities portfolio) exempt under Art. 5A(8); foreign real estate is outside Greek inheritance tax anyway. Brackets apply to Greek-situs assets only.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Exemption tied to the regime (maximum 15 tax years); after it ends, a Greek-resident's foreign movables fall back into the standard scope.

income.name: Greece

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax on employment, business and pension income: 9% to EUR 10,000, 20% to 20,000, 26% to 30,000, 34% to 40,000, 39% to 60,000 and 44% above (scale as listed by PwC after Law 5246/2025, in force from 1 January 2026). Employees pay 13.37% EFKA contributions up to a monthly ceiling of EUR 7,761.94; the self-employed pay fixed monthly amounts by insurance category.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Fixed EFKA amounts from 1 January 2026 per insurance category (main pension + health in kind + health in cash, EUR a month; ministerial decision D.15/D'/1865/2026 as shown on TaxHeaven, where e.g. 6th category = 597.06 + 7.16 + 71.65): 1st 250.77, 2nd 300.93, 3rd 360.63, 4th 433.47, 5th 519.45, 6th 675.87. The 6th (top) category is EUR 8,110.44 a year, i.e. about 15.0% of EUR 54,000; the 1st category is EUR 3,009 a year, about 5.6% of EUR 54,000. The recorded 16% up to EUR 50,690 is a derived equivalent of the TOP category (it reproduces EUR 8,110.44 at any income above EUR 50,690), a conservative assumption: the TaxHeaven page does not say how a category is assigned (by choice or by income), and supplementary-pension and lump-sum contributions are extra. Reduced tax scales apply to those under 30 and with children (not modelled). The employee tax credit was not on the pages opened and is not modelled.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax. The 2026 scale is the one on the PwC page; the page does not label the year, but the significant-developments page says Law 5246/2025 changes apply from 1 January 2026.

regimes.name: Digital nomad visa
regimes.description: National visa and residence permit for non-EU remote workers employed by or serving clients outside Greece, who may not work for a Greek company. Official portal (workfromgreece.gr): salary of at least EUR 3,500 a month AFTER TAXES (plus 20% for a spouse or cohabitant and 15% per child); visa up to one year, then a residence permit of up to two years renewable for two more. min_income is a gross equivalent: EUR 42,000 net a year needs about EUR 66,000 gross for a self-employed person in the top EFKA category (about EUR 61,000 in the lowest) and about EUR 66,800 for an employee, using the PwC 2026 scale and 13.37% contributions (our arithmetic, no tax credits). The visa does not set a tax rate; someone present over 183 days becomes a Greek tax resident taxed on worldwide income at the normal scale. The 5C regime is a separate matter and is not automatic.
regimes.duration_note: Visa up to 1 year to enter; the digital nomad residence permit is valid up to 2 years and renewable for 2 more years (workfromgreece.gr), so 4 years of permit.

regimes.name: Article 5C: relocated employees and business owners (50% exemption)
regimes.description: 50% of Greek-source employment or business income is exempt from income tax for up to seven tax years, with no extension. Requires non-residence in Greece for 5 of the previous 6 years, a transfer of tax residence from an EU/EEA state or a state with a tax administrative cooperation agreement, a new job with a Greek legal entity or a foreign company's Greek permanent establishment (or a new business), and an intention to stay at least two years. Apply by the end of the year of starting work (before 2 July) or the following year.

succession.name: Greece
succession.summary: Children, parents and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Greece has no trust law; foundations exist, but family use is unclear.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants, parents, and the surviving spouse or registered partner who would inherit on intestacy: half of the intestate portion (Civil Code art. 1825; calculation arts. 1830-1834; lifetime gift clawback within two years, arts. 1835-1838; Law 3719/2008 art. 11).
succession.foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
succession.trust_note: Greece is not a party to the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention (not in the HCCH table). Greek law has no domestic trust; the tax code treats foreign trusts as taxable entities. Foundations are governed by Civil Code arts. 108-121 and Law 4182/2013; sources suggest private purposes are possible if specific, lasting and lawful, but this is unconfirmed.
open_questions: Whether a Greek foundation may serve private family purposes (Civil Code arts. 108-121, Law 4182/2013) was not confirmed.
Greek tax treatment of foreign trusts only taken from a Mondaq headline summary.

assumptions: The family are not Greek tax residents in 7 of the 8 years before the move and invest EUR 500,000 or more in Greece (the EUR 5M home qualifies) within 3 years (art. 5A(1)).
The spouse is included in Art. 5A for EUR 20,000 a year, because she co-owns the portfolio; the three children have no foreign income and are not included.
Dividends carry 15% foreign withholding. The credit under art. 9 is capped at the Greek tax, so foreign dividends bear no Greek tax on top of the withholding.
The portfolio is in positions far below 0.5% of any listed company, so gains on listed shares are outside Greek tax (art. 42(1)(b)).

Greek inheritance tax is shown for one parent's estate of EUR 10m passing to three children; the surviving spouse's own scale and gifts in life (EUR 800,000 parental grant allowance, then 10%) are not modelled.

Structures considered and rejected: a Greek holding company taxes portfolio dividends and share gains as business income at the corporate rate (the participation exemption needs a 10% stake held 24 months), which is worse than 5% and 0; Greece has not ratified the Hague Trusts Convention and taxes trusts and foundations by look-through (circular POL 1114/2017), so no family trust or foundation path is offered.
open_questions: Whether the 0.5% test for gains on listed shares (art. 42(1)(b)) is meant to cover shares listed on foreign (non-EU) exchanges: the article speaks of a stock market without naming Greek ones, and no guidance was found. Assumed yes, as in the tax file.

Whether the tax authority takes the EUR 20,000 relative supplement for a spouse who holds half the portfolio, or whether the spouse is also taxed on her own foreign income if she is not included: assumed she is included.
Greek corporate tax rate (22%) and the details of circular POL 1114/2017 were not opened in the primary text; the structure rejection rests on PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries and secondary summaries.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Dividends 5% (Law 4172/2013 art. 40(1)), with the 15% foreign withholding credited up to the Greek tax (art. 9), so foreign dividends bear no extra Greek tax; gains on listed shares are outside tax below a 0.5% holding (art. 42(1)(b)); no wealth tax. A foreign portfolio of a Greek-resident deceased passes under the Category A scale (EUR 150,000 free per child, then 1% / 5% / 10%).

paths.name: Art. 5A flat tax (EUR 100,000 + EUR 20,000 for the spouse, 15 years)
paths.regime: Art. 5A alternative taxation of foreign income (EUR 100,000 flat)
paths.note: EUR 100,000 a year on all foreign income plus EUR 20,000 for the spouse (art. 5A(2)), for 15 tax years, then the standard rules. Needs EUR 500,000 invested in Greece within 3 years (art. 5A(1)); the family's EUR 5M Greek home meets it. Foreign movable property passing to the children is exempt from inheritance and gift tax (art. 5A(8)), but the 15-year limit means the deaths in years 30 and 60 fall under the standard rules.

immigration.name: Greece
immigration.summary: EU citizens only register. Non-EU citizens (US and others) can buy property from EUR 250,000 to EUR 800,000 depending on type and area for a 5-year Golden Visa, invest EUR 250,000 in a start-up, or qualify as financially independent (EUR 42,000 a year, 183 days of presence) or as digital nomads (EUR 42,000 a year of remote income).
immigration.naturalisation: 7 years of lawful residence, Greek language (B1 or higher) and civics tests; shorter paths (3 years) for some categories such as EU citizens and spouses of Greek citizens. A search result described an EU long-term residence permit becoming a precondition after 7 years, with transitional rules, but its date could not be confirmed (open question). The Golden Visa does not shorten the 7 years.

routes.summary: EU citizens may live in Greece and register after 3 months.
routes.requirements: Valid ID or passport. Beyond 3 months, register as worker, self-employed, student or economically inactive with resources and health cover. Permanent right of residence after 5 years (Directive 2004/38).
routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 183-day or centre-of-vital-interests test.

routes.name: Golden Visa: real estate
routes.summary: A 5-year renewable permit for buying one property of at least 120 m2: EUR 800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and large islands, EUR 400,000 elsewhere.
routes.requirements: Single property of at least 120 m2 (smaller units can no longer be combined). EUR 800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and islands with more than 3,100 residents (one source says 3,000); EUR 400,000 elsewhere; EUR 250,000 for converting commercial property to residential or restoring listed buildings (no minimum area). Short-term letting of the property is restricted. Higher thresholds took effect in 2024 (exact date not sourced).
routes.investment_options: EUR 250,000 conversion/restoration; EUR 400,000 standard; EUR 800,000 in high-demand areas. See golden_visa_financial for non-property options.
routes.processing_time: Usually a few months; a submission certificate lets you stay while pending.
routes.family: Spouse, children up to 21 and parents of both spouses.
routes.tax_note: The permit does not make you tax resident unless you spend more than 183 days a year in Greece.

routes.summary: Alternatives to property: EUR 350,000 in a Greek mutual fund up to EUR 800,000 in listed securities, with a EUR 500,000 deposit, bonds or company shares in between.
routes.requirements: Per Immigrant Invest: mutual or alternative funds from EUR 350,000; Greek bank term deposit, Greek company share capital, or Greek government bonds EUR 500,000; hotel or timeshare lease (10 years) EUR 400,000; exchange-traded securities EUR 800,000. Mondaq and other pages quote slightly different figures (EUR 400,000 for funds or bonds), so verify with the Ministry of Migration and Asylum.
routes.investment_options: Hotel or timeshare lease EUR 400,000; deposit, company shares or government bonds EUR 500,000; listed securities EUR 800,000.
routes.family: Spouse, children up to 21 and parents of both spouses.
routes.tax_note: The permit does not make you tax resident unless you spend more than 183 days a year in Greece.

routes.name: Start-up investor residence permit
routes.summary: EUR 250,000 into a start-up registered in the Elevate Greece national registry, with a cap on your stake.
routes.requirements: Share-capital increase or bonds worth at least EUR 250,000; holding at most 33% of capital or votes; the start-up must create at least 2 full-time jobs in year one and keep staffing for 5 years. Permit duration is reported both as 1 year then 2-year renewals and as 5 years. Start date reported as 1 January 2025 (not confirmed against the statute).

sources.title: Greece Now Offers EUR 250K Startup Visa

routes.name: Financially Independent Person (FIP) permit
routes.summary: For retirees and others living on stable income from abroad of at least EUR 3,500 a month; no work in Greece.
routes.requirements: Stable passive income (pensions, rent, dividends) from outside Greece of EUR 3,500 a month, i.e. EUR 42,000 a year; +20% for a spouse, +15% per child. Alternative reported: EUR 126,000 savings. Health insurance. 3-year permit, renewable. At least 183 days a year in Greece, checked at renewal. Legal basis reported as Law 5038/2023 (not verified).
routes.fees_note: Visa EUR 180 + permit application EUR 1,000 + card EUR 16, per Immigrant Invest; the source also lists a EUR 150 administrative fee.
routes.physical_presence: At least 183 days a year; no absence over 6 consecutive months
routes.family: Spouse and children via the income uplift.
routes.tax_note: Living in Greece 183+ days makes you tax resident. The source says this permit does not lead directly to permanent residence or citizenship unless converted; treat years as unclear.

sources.title: Greece FIP vs Golden Visa

routes.name: Digital nomad visa and residence permit
routes.summary: For remote workers earning EUR 3,500 a month from non-Greek clients or employers.
routes.requirements: Income EUR 3,500 a month (gross or net unclear, sources differ), +20% spouse, +15% per child. Health insurance, clean record, accommodation. Since 5 February 2026 (Law 5275/2026) apply at a Greek consulate before travel. D visa 12 months, then a 2-year permit, renewable in 2-year periods.
routes.fees_note: Visa about EUR 75 and residence permit EUR 1,000, per Remote Work Europe; another source quotes different figures.
routes.physical_presence: No minimum sourced; 183+ days makes you tax resident
routes.family: Family members get permits of the same validity and need their own insurance.
routes.tax_note: 50% income tax exemption for up to 7 years if you move tax residence to Greece and were not resident in 5 of the previous 6 years.

routes.name: Work permits (employment, seasonal, highly qualified)
routes.summary: Non-EU workers need an employer, a work visa and a residence permit; the EU Blue Card covers highly qualified staff.
routes.requirements: Employer-led process under the migration code; details and quotas not researched in depth.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Greece; no fixed day count sourced
